_comment: Atlas — единая карта знаний и подходов playdisplay. Источник: PlayDisplay_Атлас_единая_структура_v2.docx. Тип задаёт роль карточки: Принцип — как мы думаем, Технология — чем это делается, Наблюдение — что мы видим у посетителей, Приём — как это применяется, Исследование — куда смотрим дальше. Готовых идей решений здесь нет намеренно: они живут в библиотеке (data/concepts.json), Атлас — про слои знания. Сейчас все карточки — тезисы: читаются в сетке и не кликаются. Если у карточки появятся principle и examples, она сама начнёт открываться в разбор — рендер это поддерживает.

items.title: Designers don't decorate — they find the form of the solution
items.desc: Expression is never laid on top of function. It grows out of the problem itself: how people behave, what the space is like, what the project's limits are, and which technologies are chosen.

items.title: The future already exists as options
items.desc: Inspiration is the moment a designer notices one of the possible futures before anyone else does. Value appears when that option can be turned into a real object, space or experience.

items.title: Flow demands total attention
items.desc: Strong solutions rarely arrive in passing. The designer goes all the way into the problem, notices connections, discards the obvious answers and holds the idea until it takes exact form.

items.title: Technology guarantees nothing
items.desc: The same technology can create a powerful experience or stay expensive equipment. Value appears when it becomes part of a precise idea.

items.title: Every constraint makes the idea stronger
items.desc: Budget, schedule, architecture, safety and existing equipment apply the pressure that an exact solution is born out of.

items.title: Space is a language
items.desc: Light, scale, path, sound and movement tell the story before any text does.

items.title: The best ideas look inevitable
items.desc: Once it is built, it seems there was no other way. That effect appears when a difficult problem has been solved with real precision.

items.title: Complexity belongs backstage
items.desc: The more natural an interaction feels, the more work is usually hidden inside the project.

items.title: We design behavior
items.desc: Screens, projectors and software can be bought. The real work is designing how people will move, stop, wonder and interact.

items.title: The experience begins before the first step
items.desc: A project starts with anticipation and ends with a memory. The entrance, the queue and the first glance already shape how the experience is received.

items.title: A good idea brings people together
items.desc: A strong project starts a conversation: people point out details to each other, take photos, laugh and come back together.

items.title: Real magic leaves questions
items.desc: When people want a second look, want to walk around it and check their own senses, the impression stays with them.

items.title: Memory keeps moments you lived through
items.desc: Facts fade fast. Personal experience, surprise and emotion go on living in memory.

items.title: Surprise opens attention
items.desc: Surprise creates a pause in which a person is ready to look, listen and explore further.

items.title: The best technology disappears
items.desc: When visitors talk about the experience and not the equipment, the technology has done its job.

items.title: Design is a way of making decisions
items.desc: Design starts with the question of what a person should feel and do, then builds form, narrative and technology around that answer.

items.title: Constraints are the best co-author
items.desc: Expression often comes about because of a project's limits, not in spite of them.

items.title: A good idea looks obvious once someone has had it
items.desc: Precision hides the search behind it and makes the result feel natural.

items.title: Creativity is the ability to see a connection
items.desc: A strong idea joins together elements that until then were seen separately.

items.title: Every project starts with a feeling
items.desc: First we decide what a person should feel. Then we build everything that helps them live it.

items.title: Virtual reality for training
items.desc: VR makes it safe to rehearse difficult and rare situations, repeat scenarios and get instant feedback.

items.title: Generative graphics
items.desc: The image is created in real time and changes in response to a person, to data or to the state of the space.

items.title: Computer vision
items.desc: Cameras read movement, position and action, turning natural behavior into a way of controlling things.

items.title: Spatial sound
items.desc: Sound builds direction, depth and a sense of presence, tying a virtual event to a physical place.

items.title: Sensor systems
items.desc: Movement, touch, voice and body position become inputs for the scenario.

items.title: People rarely retell facts
items.desc: But they almost always retell the moments that surprised them.

items.title: Architecture speaks first
items.desc: People read scale, light, form and route before any text appears.

items.title: Space can guide without signage
items.desc: Light, sound, perspective and movement suggest the next step on their own.

items.title: Simplicity usually hides a lot of work
items.desc: The more natural an interaction looks, the more carefully the scenario and the technology behind it were worked out.

items.title: If people discuss the equipment, the idea has lost
items.desc: If they discuss what they felt and lived through, the technology worked.

items.title: A shared emotion is stronger than a private one
items.desc: People remember an experience better when they have shared it with others.

items.title: Watching can be as good as taking part
items.desc: Participants' reactions can become part of the show and draw in the people around them.

items.title: A personal action changes what the experience is worth
items.desc: Whatever a person has influenced themselves feels more significant to them.

items.title: A space people want to photograph
items.desc: A strong installation tells a person where to stop and what to do. The photograph becomes part of the narrative, and the experience travels further.

items.title: Give adults their curiosity back
items.desc: Play briefly removes status, job title and habitual seriousness. A person explores, tries things and enjoys discovery again.

items.title: Magic is stronger than technology
items.desc: Visitors care more about the moment of the impossible than about how it is done. A real object comes alive, an image appears in mid-air, familiar physics changes.

items.title: Several technologies, one effect
items.desc: Light, sound, mechanics, graphics and sensors all work at once, but read as a single whole event.

items.title: The visitor becomes a participant
items.desc: The story turns personal when a visitor affects what happens through movement, voice or choice.

items.title: Better together
items.desc: A shared task turns a group into a team and creates a memory they hold in common.

items.title: The experience begins in the queue
items.desc: An installation is worth watching from the outside, not only going through. Other people's reactions build the intrigue.

items.title: Surprise first, explain after
items.desc: The first effect opens attention. After that a complex story can be told in real depth.

items.title: The action has to feel natural
items.desc: Step up, look in, touch, turn, jump — the clearer the first gesture, the faster a person enters the experience.

items.title: The story continues after the exit
items.desc: A photograph, a game result, an image someone made or simply retelling it all extend the life of the experience.

items.title: Every visitor goes through their own story
items.desc: One space can offer different routes, choices and depths of interaction.

items.title: The real thing begins where the screens end
items.desc: When media become part of the architecture, the light, the objects and the movement, the space reads as one whole.

items.title: Memory loves the unexpected
items.desc: Moments that break expectations stay with people longer than a consistent explanation.

items.title: Virtual worlds instead of websites
items.desc: A browser can become a space for travel, presentation, learning or acting together.

items.title: Personal sound in a public space
items.desc: Directional audio systems make individual sound scenarios possible without headphones.

items.title: The dome as a window
items.desc: A vertical hemisphere creates a different kind of immersion: you are not looking up, you are looking through an opening into another environment.

items.title: Personalizing the space
items.desc: One place can change its content, its language and its level of difficulty for the particular visitor in front of it.
